questions.q: Where does the imperfect stem come from?
choices: The nous form of the present, minus -ons
The ils form of the present, minus -ent
The je form of the present
questions.why: Nous parlons → parl-, nous finissons → finiss-, nous buvons → buv-. Because the stem is taken from a real present-tense form, even wild irregulars behave.

questions.q: How many verbs have an irregular imperfect in French?
questions.why: Être has no -ons stem to work from, so it uses ét-: j'étais, nous étions. Everything else follows the nous rule exactly.
Nous finissons gives the stem finiss-, and the nous ending is -ions: finissions. The -iss- belongs to the stem, not to the ending.
The one irregular stem in the language: ét- plus the ordinary endings. J'étais, tu étais, il était, nous étions.
Nous faisons → fais-, so faisait. The spelling keeps the ai even though this stem is not pronounced the way it looks.

questions.q: Which imperfect of « manger » is correct?
questions.why: The e of -ger is only there to soften the g before a or o. The nous ending is -ions, which starts with i, so the e is dropped: nous mangions. Compare je mangeais, where it must stay.
The cedilla keeps the c soft before a: commençait. It disappears in nous commencions, where the i already softens it.
The stem étudi- already ends in i, and the ending -ions adds another: étudiions. It looks like a typo and is correct, exactly like nous riions.

questions.q: Why is « Elle avait vingt ans » in the imperfect?
choices: Because it happened once and finished
Because age is a state, and the imperfect describes
Because avoir has no passé composé
questions.why: The imperfect answers what was going on, never what happened next. Age, weather, feelings and appearance are all states, so they live in the imperfect.

questions.q: In speech, what separates « je parlais » from « je parlerai » ?
choices: An extra r sound in the future
questions.why: The future is built on the whole infinitive, so parlerai carries a second r that parlais does not. That r is the only audible difference between the two tenses.
Nous pleuvons is not used, but the stem pleuv- is what the imperfect needs. Weather is description, so it is almost always the imperfect.

questions.q: Translate: I used to live in Paris.
questions.why: Used to is the habit meaning, which is one of the imperfect's three jobs. French has no separate used to construction: the tense carries it.

questions.q: Build the suggestion: How about going to the cinema?
questions.why: Si plus the imperfect, with no second half, is a fixed way of proposing something. Nothing about it is past.

questions.q: Say this out loud: the weather was nice.
questions.why: Faire in the imperfect is the standard weather verb, and the -ait ending is the same sound as -ais and -aient.

questions.q: Name the three jobs of the imperfect, with a French example each.
a: 1. Ongoing background action: Je lisais quand tu es arrivé. 2. Habit or repeated action: Quand j'étais petit, j'allais à la mer tous les étés. 3. Description of a state — weather, age, feelings, appearance: Il faisait beau / Elle avait vingt ans / J'étais fatigué.
questions.why: All three reduce to the same idea: the imperfect describes rather than narrates. Verbs of state — être, avoir, savoir, vouloir, pouvoir — default to it for that reason.
